input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The duplicate-numbered § 12.4 (p0046) imposes a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months on Customer covering any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory, with no carve-outs — walk-away territory under the rule and a failure of the fallback on scope, duration and carve-outs. It also contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. The smallest operative cure at the preferred level is flipping the prohibitory operator ("shall not" to "may"), which leaves no non-compete and no field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer while keeping every other word intact; a narrowed term-only restriction on a single named product is offered in the comment only. The separate no-hire covenant at p0045 is left for the applicable no-hire rule.

ops.oldText: Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire
ops.newText: Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the products, services or territories in which we develop, buy or sell, so we have flipped the § 12.4 prohibition into a permission, consistent with § 12.3. If Cobalt needs protection, we could consider a term-only restriction on a single named competing product, capped at 12 months with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Turn the 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer into a permission by changing "shall not" to "may".
